description: Doris Stanley recalls learning of the September 11, 2001 attacks while working at a restaurant that was preparing to open for lunch. She describes televisions in the restaurant switching to coverage of the attacks in New York, the Pentagon, and Pennsylvania, which the staff watched while preparing for the day. Stanley recalls watching the World Trade Center collapse live on television and feeling shocked and frightened by the repeated coverage. She connects the hours of televised coverage with anxiety and panic attacks that followed, and says counseling services at UCF helped her explore that impact. During a later trip to New York for a conference, she visited the memorial and describes the experience as healing in some ways. Recorded for the UCF Remembers 9/11 collection on September 11, 2026, her account reflects on the lasting effects of witnessing the attacks through television coverage.

entities_and_facets.perspective: Personal recollection of watching television coverage of the attacks while at work, and reflection on their lasting effects; she does not describe being physically present at an attack site.
